description: Template rendering, regex, and JSONPath transforms in a single text-utility tool.

tools.description:
Text utilities in one tool, driven by `operation`:

- `template` renders a Jinja2 `template` against `variables` (build prompts, emails, SQL, HTML).
- `regex` runs `pattern` against `text` with `mode` match/search/findall/sub/split (extract emails/ids/dates, clean/rewrite/split text).
- `json` extracts/reshapes JSON via a JSONPath `path` (single value/list) or `mapping` (`{out_field: $.json.path}`).

When to use: Any time the user asks to fill placeholders, pattern-match/extract/replace in text, or pluck/reshape fields out of a JSON blob.

How to discover inputs: If the input lives in a file and the path isn't given, FIRST call CatalogFileTool(operation='list', source_uri=...) or CatalogBrowserTool to locate it, then set `source_uri`. Every operation accepts `source_uri` (read input) and `dest_uri` (persist output); prefer these over inline `template`/`text`/`data` for stored files.

How to communicate: Return the rendered text / match list / extracted JSON verbatim in a fenced block; for large result sets summarize the count and show the first few. If output was written to `dest_uri`, mention the path in one line.

Examples: operation='template', template='Hi {{ name }}', variables='{"name":"Ada"}'. operation='regex', text='a@x.com, b@y.org', pattern='[\w.]+@[\w.]+', mode='findall'. operation='json', data='{"items":[{"id":1},{"id":2}]}', path='$.items[*].id'.

schema.name: operation
schema.description: Which utility to run. `template` renders Jinja2, `regex` runs a regular expression, `json` extracts/reshapes JSON with JSONPath.

schema.name: template
schema.description: [template] Inline Jinja2 template body, e.g. `Hello {{ name }}, you have {{ count }} items.`. Required for operation=template unless `source_uri` is provided; ignored when `source_uri` is set.
examples: Hi {{ name }}, you have {{ count }} items.
SELECT * FROM {{ table }} WHERE id = {{ id }};

schema.name: variables
schema.description: [template] JSON object whose keys are the Jinja2 variable names, e.g. `{"name":"Ada","count":3}`. Pass `{}` for templates with no variables.

schema.name: text
schema.description: [regex] Inline haystack text the regex runs against. Required for operation=regex unless `source_uri` is provided; ignored when `source_uri` is set.

schema.name: pattern
schema.description: [regex] Python regular expression, e.g. `[\w.]+@[\w.]+` for emails or `\d{4}-\d{2}-\d{2}` for ISO dates. Required for operation=regex. Use capture groups for `\1`-style backrefs in `replacement`.

schema.name: mode
schema.description: [regex] The regex operation. `match` anchors at the start, `search` finds the first hit anywhere, `findall` returns all hits (default), `sub` replaces, `split` breaks the text on the pattern. Legacy aliases `extract`->`findall` and `replace`->`sub` still work.

schema.name: replacement
schema.description: [regex] Replacement string used only when `mode='sub'`. Supports backrefs like `\1` referencing capture groups in `pattern`, e.g. `redacted-\1`.

schema.name: data
schema.description: [json] Inline JSON document, as a JSON string like `{"items":[{"id":1}]}`. Required for operation=json unless `source_uri` is provided; ignored when `source_uri` is set.

schema.name: path
schema.description: [json] Single JSONPath expression evaluated against the input, e.g. `$.items[*].id`. Use this OR `mapping`, not both.

schema.name: mapping
schema.description: [json] JSON object of `{output_field: jsonpath}` pairs used to assemble a new shape, e.g. `{"name":"$.user.name","email":"$.user.email"}`. Use this OR `path`, not both.

schema.name: source_uri
schema.description: AIDP URI to read the operation's input from (template body / regex haystack / JSON document), overriding the inline field. Format: `master:<catalog>.<schema>.<volume>:/<path>` or `workspace:/<path>`.

schema.name: dest_uri
schema.description: Optional AIDP URI to persist the primary output (rendered text / match results as JSON / transformed JSON). Same URI grammar as `source_uri`. The result is still returned in the response envelope.

_confDescriptions.autoescape: [template] Jinja2 autoescape toggle. true escapes HTML-sensitive chars; false (default) leaves them as-is.
_confDescriptions.strict: [template] If true, undefined template variables raise an error. If false (default), they render as empty strings.
_confDescriptions.multiline: [regex] Multiline mode (re.MULTILINE): ^ and $ match at line boundaries. Default false.
_confDescriptions.max_matches: [regex] Cap on matches returned by findall/split to prevent runaway output. Default 500.
_confDescriptions.max_input_bytes: [json] Cap on input JSON size in bytes; oversized input is rejected. Default 1048576 (1 MiB).
_confDescriptions.max_results: [json] Cap on JSONPath matches returned to prevent runaway output. Default 1000.
_confDescriptions.source_uri: Optional input URI. Accepts master:<catalog>.<schema>.<volume>:/<path>, workspace:/<path>, or the bare <catalog>.<schema>.<volume>:/<path> alias. When set, overrides the inline input parameter for the chosen operation.
_confDescriptions.dest_uri: Optional output URI for the primary result. Accepts the same URI formats as source_uri. Writing the destination does not suppress the result in the response envelope.
